The North Quays main contract has progressed well over the summer. 
With the removal of the cofferdams the substructure, bridge 
abutments and piers for the Sustainable Transport Bridge are now 
visible.  The fabrication of the steel deck superstructure in Belgium is 
near completion, and the mechanical and electrical components are 
currently being installed.  Works are also progressing on the new 
public plaza on the South Quays and the bridge plant room.
The Transport Hub building works has progressed to roof level, enclosing the concourse area that will also house the 
ticketing area and offi ces at fi rst fl oor level.  Works to the platforms and rail track are continuing and ground works have 
commenced on the new pedestrian access bridge to the west of the Transport Hub.   
Demolition of Hump bank bridge / OBH 127 to allow 
for western pedestrian bridge construction  Road 
and access infrastructure is progressing well, and 
traffi c management measures continue to be in 
place.  Works are continuing along Fountain Street 
and works has also focused on Abbey Road while 
the schools were closed.  The realigned Abbey Road 
is taking shape with access to a new dedicated 
school access lane and set down area.  
New entrance walls and gates are currently being 
constructed with a new staff parking area and play 
courts being provided for the Our Lady of Good 
Council National School.   
Current arrangement for Abbey Road 
The aerial image illustrates the signifi cant progress 
and improvements that have taken place on Abbey 
Road over the summer and identifi es the various 
elements that make up the overall layout. 
  
Works are continuing on the various bridge 
structures, retaining and boundary walls.  The decks 
for the greenway underpasses are also in place.      
Construction on the new railway fl ood defence 
system will commence this quarter. This system will 
protect the existing and new rail infrastructure from 
the increasing impacts of fl ooding, future proof and 
ensure a climate resilient commuter rail service.

TOURISM 
Waterford Rural Tourism Network 
The Waterford Rural Tourism Network (WRTN) is continuing to develop. Since the beginning of 2024 workshops, 
learning journeys and meetings have been delivered by Runda Hospitality & Tourism Solutions on behalf of Waterford 
City & County Council. Before the end of 2024 there will be further trainings provided which includes in-person meetings 
LEO Webinars, 2nd Learning Journey, Failte Ireland lead trainings, Sptlight Series continued & Newtworking event day 
in November. If you are aware of any businesses who could benefit from being involved, please put them in touch with 
Orna Holohan, Tourism Officer.
DEDP Implementation Group
As the Waterford Destination & Experience Development Plan (DEDP) nears completion a stakeholder Implementation 
Group has been established to ensure the tourism industry has a clear voice in the delivery of projects identified in the 
plan. Two meetings have taken place to date with the third scheduled for the end of October.
Water-Sports Activity Facility Centre Development 
Significant funding from Fáilte Ireland has been secured and plans have been updated for the inclusion of Changing 
Places Facilities.
Ireland From Above Filming
A new 6-part series being filmed in Ireland for broadcast on PBS in the US has commenced filming in Waterford. Two 
of a four days filming, mostly filmed using a drone, has taken place in Waterford. When filming is complete, a full 25min 
episode showcasing the intriguing stories and sites of interest in Waterford City and County will be broadcast to millions 
of viewers in the US (likely in Q1 2025).

Management Report Plenary 13th September 2024.
Forward Planning Report
Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) Draft Annual Revised Map
On the 1st day of February last, Waterford City and County Council prepared and published the RZLT draft annual 
revised map for the 2025 tax liability year. The following stages and timeline apply to the annual mapping process:
1.Publication of a draft annual revised map followed by a 2-month period of public consultation, accompanied by place-
ment of advertisements in local press and across Waterford Council social media accounts;
2.Receipt of written submissions from landowners and consideration thereof;
3.Notification of written determinations made by Waterford Council to the relevant landowners who made written submis-
sions to the draft map;
4.Making of appeals to An Bord Pleanála where landowners are aggrieved by the determination of the council; and,
5.Publication of final annual revised map at the start of the relevant tax liability year followed by a repeat of the pro-
cess to prepare a new draft annual revised map. We are currently in stage 4 in this timeline and have been notified of 
two appeals to An Bord Pleanála relating to our determinations to retain lands as in-scope for the purposes of the tax. 
Following decisions being made by An Bord Pleanála on these cases, we will proceed to publish the final annual map in 
early 2025. 
Development Plan and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA)Monitoring
We are actively compiling an update to last year’s development plan and core strategy monitoring report which we circu-
lated to the plenary council and the Office of the Planning Regulator in September 2023. This year however, the updated 
report will be the mid-term development plan report required under Section 15(2) of the Planning and Development 
Act 2000, as amended and will be accompanied by the 2-year Strategic Environmental Assessment monitoring report 
required pursuant to Article 13J of the Planning and Development (Strategic Environmental Assessment) Regulations 
2004. The reports will now be completed and shared with the council in October. The reports are important documents 
which will inform further discussion with both the Planning SPC and the Plenary council on any changes required to 
support full implementation of the plan.  
High Court Decision on Judicial Review in the case of Ruden Homes Ltd & John Deane (Applicants) and Waterford City 
& County Council (Respondents). (2022 651 JR)
An ex parte application was made to the High Court by Ruden Homes and John Deane on the 5th day of September 
2022, for leave to apply for a Judicial Review of the process for the making of the Waterford City and County
Development Plan 2022-2028. By order of the court, leave was granted to seek a number of reliefs while the court
further granted a stay in respect of the coming into force of the Waterford City and County Development Plan 2022-2028 
in respect of the zoning of lands owned and controlled by John Deane and Ruden Homes Limited at Monang, 
Dungarvan.On Wednesday 10th day of July last, the High Court made the following order in this case as it relates to the 
Waterford City & County Development Plan 2022 – 2028: An Order of Certiorari quashing the decision of the 
Respondent of the 7th June 2022 to make the Material Alteration Amendment No.213 and the Amendment in respect 
of DGD022 in the Waterford City and County Council Development Plan 2022-2028 as such Amendments relate to the 
Lands at Monang, Dungarvan, Co. Waterford as identified in paragraph 3 of the Affidavit of John Deane sworn on the 
23rd day of July 2022.In effect, the court ordered that the land use zoning applied to the respondent’s land be 
consistent with what had been identified in the draft development plan, setting aside the amendments applied to the 
lands in the latter stage of the development plan preparation process, while the specific development objective relating 
to the lands also be deleted from the development plan. For reference, set out hereunder is the text of specific develop-
ment objective DGD022 which the High Court has ordered be deleted from Volume 3, Appendix 2 of the Development 
Plan. In addition, a map is attached hereunder which outlines the lands at Monang which are the subject of the High 
Court Order, and which are now in accordance with that order, zoned for “New Residential Development” (GZT R1). 
Since the date of the court decision, the changes to the development plan text have duly been made while the mapping 
changes are being undertaken. All prescribed authorities consulted with during the preparation of the development plan, 
including the OPR and An Bord Pleanála have also been notified of the court decision. Text now deleted from Volume 3, 
Appendix 3 of the Waterford City and County Development Plan 2022-2028.

Heritage Offi cer Report 
Heritage Week 2024
Heritage Week this year ran from August 17th-25th with over 60 events taking place across Waterford City and County 
and record attendances at several events.  Events hosted by Waterford City and County Council included talks on Wa-
terford Placenames, the 1925 Gaeltacht Commission and the Woodstown Viking Festival which attracted around 1,400 
attendees over the weekend. Digital projects included the launch of a GIS Story Map about St. John’s River available to 
view on  https://www.heritageweek.ie/projects/st-johns-pill-waterford . 
Decade of Commemorations
The launch of The Aftermath, a fi lm by John Foley and funded by Waterford City and Council Commemorations Commit-
tee takes place on Tuesday, September 10th. The Aftermath captures the memories and thoughts of Waterford people 
talking about their ancestors involved in the War of Independence and the Civil War. The documentary fi lm looks at 
some of the key events and the people involved and also looks at what happened to those involved in the decades fol-
lowing the period. The fi lm was funded through the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltact, Sports and Media’s 
Decade of Commemorations Fund.    
Monastic Lismore Seminar
A Seminar on Monastic Lismore will take place on Saturday, November 16th in Lismore Heritage Centre. The seminar 
will explore the part played by Lismore and its surrounding region along the Blackwater Valley in the story of medieval 
Irish monasticism, communicating recent scholarly work on Irish monasticism in accessible and informal presenta-
tions.  The seminar builds on the recent publication of Monasticism in Ireland AD900–1250 by Waterford based Dr. Edel 
Bhreathnach. The seminar is free of charge, but pre-booking is required on Eventbrite.
Heritage Plan Grant Scheme
Projects allocated funding by the Heritage Council’s Heritage Plan Fund are progressing well.

Conservation Offi cer Report
Built Heritage Investment Scheme (BHIS) 2024 and the Historic Structures Fund (HSF) 2024 
This year Waterford has received funding of €506,400 for built heritage. €242,400 has been provided for 27 projects for 
private and public buildings in the city and county under the BHIS scheme. This will support works such as   the repair 
of historic roofs, walls and chimneys, repair of joinery and repair of historic stained glass . This funding also includes 
€73,793 which has been ring- fenced specifi cally for 6 thatch house projects.
  
Under the Historic Structure Fund €264,000 has been allocated for 4 projects. The  call for BHIS funding for 2025 has 
also been brought forward to  this year, and closing dates for applications is 27th of September. The earlier closing date 
will mean that the owners and contractors will have additional time to do works. Full details  of the scheme, including the 
application form, a guidance document for applicants and list of eligible works are available at:
https://waterfordcouncil.ie/documents/grants/#built-heritage-funding-2025 
The Irish language versions of the An Scéim Infheistíochta don Oidhreacht Thógtha (BHIS) 2025 Circular and Applica-

Biodiversity Officer
Waterford Biodiversity Action Plan – Preparation Stage
The Waterford Biodiversity Action Plan is in the development phase. This process will continue over the course of 2024 
and into early 2025. 
-The meeting of the Biodiversity Working Group was delayed over July/August due to the volume of expert members on 
holidays. This will resume in September.
-Further mapping, updated research papers, new biodiversity data and additional rare species data was compiled to 
inform the priority areas for the WBAP. 
-Had regular discussions with NPWS and NBDC on the opportunities and challenges for biodiversity in the county.
-Survey for public engagement at the pre-draft stage is in development. This will invite the public to have their say on the 
upcoming plan.
-Public meetings in all MDs will take place in October and November 2024 for public input.
National Biodiversity Webinar Series
In conjunction with Mariana Colman, An Taisce National Climate Ambassadors Programme Coordinator produced the 
Not Stopping Now! Nature’s Resilience webinar series.  Aimed at a public audience nationally as a collaboration be-
tween WCCC, the national Biodiversity Officer Network, the Heritage Council and Climate Ambassadors.
Advertised nationally on social media channels, within councils and through the Climate Ambassadors newsletter with 
121 sign-ups to Episode 1.  Episode 1 on Pollinators streamed live on 24th July 1-2p.m. in collaboration with the Na-
tional Biodiversity Data Centre and Kerry Co Co Biodiversity Officer, Eleanor Turner.  The series will stream 4 episodes 
in total over 4 months inc. topics Pollinators, Bats, Birds and Dark Skies in collaboration with NBDC, Bat Conservation 
Ireland, BirdWatch Ireland and Dark Sky Ireland.
Episode 2 on Bats was delivered by Karen Healy of Bat Conservation Ireland and presented by Marina Mulligan 
(WCCC), Monica Mullins (An Taisce) and Ruth Hanniffy (Sligo CoCo Biodiversity Officer).

AGE WELL EXPO 
The second Age Well Expo is taking place in the Park Hotel Dungarvan on Tuesday Oct 01st which will coincide with 
Positive Aging Week.
The Age Friendly Waterford event, in association with Healthy Waterford, UPMC Whitfield and Waterford City and County 
Council will showcase supports and activities available to older people to lead fulfilling, healthy and active lives.   As with 
the expo held earlier this year there will be featured talks from keynote speakers and interviews with local organisations 
and community groups providing insightful and topical information to everyone who strives to age well.  
We hope to have the same level of exhibitors as we had in May including representation from Waterford City and County 
Council to showcase support services available, such as housing grants, community engagement initiatives, energy cost 
reduction, recreational activities tailored for older adults and more. 
DEMENTIA BUS
Age Friendly Waterford, Healthy Waterford, and Waterford City and County Council are hosting a Virtual Dementia Train-
ing event on September 4th, 5th, and 6th. This training will provide local healthcare professionals, social workers, care-
givers and those interested in learning more about dementia a unique opportunity to experience firsthand the challenges 
faced by individuals living with dementia.
Virtual Dementia Training is a ground-breaking program that allows participants to simulate the cognitive and sensory 
impairments associated with dementia. By wearing specialized equipment, participants can experience first-hand the dif-
ficulties individuals with dementia face, including disorientation, confusion, and memory loss. This immersive experience 
provides valuable insights into the daily challenges faced by those living with dementia and their caregivers, fostering 
empathy, understanding, and improved care delivery.
HEALTHY WATERFORD: (WELL WATERFORD)
Healthy Waterford, a subgroup of the Local Community Development Committee (LCDC) (Well Waterford), is dedicated 
to enhancing the health and well-being of Waterford residents. This year, they’ve championed a variety of initiatives, 
including:
CONNECTING COMMUNITY ROADSHOWS 
These collaborative events, which brought together over 30 agencies in rural and urban areas from February to the end 
of May, have been nominated for a Chambers Excellence in local government award. The events showcased Waterford’s 
vibrant community services and provided invaluable guidance on setting up community groups, securing funding, and 
building stronger communities.

CLIMATE ACTION
Energy efficient streetlight replacements
Crews have begun to replace street lighting with LED equivalents that will reduce energy consumption by 70%. These 
lights will also have a longer life than the lights we currently have. All of our streetlights will be replaced by 2026.
Environmental Education & Awareness
Waste prevention
Circular Living month  - globally more textiles are consumed than ever before and Ireland is no exception. An EPA study 
carried out by researchers at MTU in 2019 found that the per capita consumption of new textiles in Ireland is 53 kg per 
person per year – that’s almost 1 kg/week of new textiles purchased by every citizen. During October there is a national 
focus on the circular economy for Circular Living month. We be placing an emphasis on repair and reuse during this 
month. There will be a series of 4 weekly workshops to teach participants sewing repair for clothes.  There will also be a 
sewing repair demonstration and a clothes swap event.
Greening food festivals: the two rinse stations are to be used again at this year’s Harvest Festival and Vitamin Sea Festi-
val to encourage the use of reusable cups, cutlery, plates, etc this  September. This was particularly useful at the food trail 
and picnic elements of the festivals. Harvest festival also had water refills available using Refill Ireland’s hydration station 
and a bin collecting plastic drinks bottles and cans for charity in conjunction with Re-turn.
Reuse at Waterford Walls – Renew Enterprises repurpose paint from our two civic amenity sites to create good quality 
paint to prevent it being sent for disposal. Thanks to their partnership with the Paint Reuse Network, they  are able to 
reduce waste and provide our communities with high quality, low impact and affordable paint, as well as preventing waste. 
This paint will feature on one of the murals in the Waterford Walls festival this year. In this first year of reusing and recycling 
paint, Waterford Walls reused and recycled approximately 125 litres of paint.

LITTER 
The Gum Litter Taskforce (GLT) took to the streets of Waterford on 2nd August. The interactive roadshow carried out fun 
and engaging education and awareness initiatives that demonstrate the proper means of gum disposal and raise 
awareness of the environmental and fiscal impacts of gum litter. The campaign is a collaboration between Food Drink 
Ireland, the Department of Environment, Climate and Communications, the chewing gum industry, and local authorities. 
This campaign was launched by the Deputy Mayor of Waterford City and County Council Cllr. Adam Wyse. 87% of people 
now report proper gum disposal, versus 49% when the campaign began in 2007– an increase of 77.5%, demonstrating 
the positive impact the campaign has had on attitudes towards gum litter. Peer pressure was found to be the key 
contributor to this shift in attitudes, followed by knowledge of the €150 fine. However, work remains to be done to further 
reduce this figure, as still only 46% of people can claim to have never dropped gum on the ground, demonstrating the 
continued importance of the awareness and behavioural change campaign. 
Community Clean-Ups
Waterford City & County Council facilitates community clean ups throughout the year to clean up litter and illegally 
dumped waste from approach roads, local beauty spots, beaches and general public areas. We continue to supply bags, 
gloves and litter pickers to many of the groups taking part. Collection of any bags of litter is then organised for after the 
clean-up takes place. 
Leave No Trace 
A Leave No Trace workshop will be held on 21st September for community groups and individuals. This hands-on session 
is aimed at educating participants on the principles of responsible outdoor ethics. During the workshop, attendees learn 
about the seven Leave No Trace principles, focusing on practical techniques to minimise their environmental impact while 
enjoying nature. The workshop includes discussions, demonstrations, and activities that cover topics like proper waste 
disposal, respecting wildlife, and sustainable camping practices. The workshop equips participants with the knowledge 
and skills to promote environmental stewardship and preserve Ireland’s natural landscapes
SCHOOLS 
The Green Schools programme for the new school year is under way once again. Approximately 61 schools are due 
to renew a Green Flag during this school year across Co. Waterford. Along with school visits, there will be webinars for 
Primary Schools and Secondary Schools in early October. These will be held for each theme of the programme e.g. 
waste, litter, water, biodiversity, travel, etc and take place online in the evening. These webinars are designed to support 
secondary school teachers and students as they work through their current theme.  The majority of teachers find online 
seminars to be a convenient way to learn about their current Green Schools theme as it eliminates travel time to and from 
the seminar. The Environmental Awareness Officer will be available to visit schools or answer any questions which they 
might have.
Composting in Schools programme – a further 8 secondary schools throughout Co. Waterford will receive a food 
waste prevention and recycling programme designed to identify ways for the school to reduce the amount of waste being 
produced and increase recycling and composting. This involves 2 visits to the schools to carry out a waste audit to help 
schools to prevent, reduce and reuse their waste. There is a strong focus on food waste. Schools can also take part in 5 
online sessions to learn more about waste prevention, recycling and composting within a school. During the last school 
year, this resulted in 7 of the 8 schools reducing the amount of waste being sent to landfill, 5 of the 8 signed up for a 
brown bin collection to compost food waste, 3 leaf cages were installed to compost leaves on school grounds and staff 
and students learned about the importance of waste prevention and recycling. 
Picker Pals – this is a litter programme for 6-9 year old focussed on their local environment. It engages with classrooms 
to create litter picking adventures at home and encourages children to share that experience with their classmates. We 
fund 10 of the schools taking part in this programme in Co. Waterford.
